question: Which of the following metals reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to produce hydrogen gas?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Zinc**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Zinc (Zn)** is a moderately reactive metal that reacts readily with **dilute Hydrochloric acid (HCl)** to produce **Zinc Chloride (ZnCl₂)** and evolve **Hydrogen gas (H₂)**.
 
• This reaction is a classic example of a **single displacement reaction**, where a more reactive metal displaces hydrogen from an acid. The chemical equation for this process is: **Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂**. ***Hence, the option Zinc is correct.***
 
• In the **reactivity series** of metals, **Zinc** is positioned above **Hydrogen**. This higher position indicates that it has a greater tendency to lose electrons and undergo **oxidation** compared to hydrogen.
 
• During the reaction, **Zinc atoms** lose two electrons to form **Zn²⁺ ions** (oxidation), while **Hydrogen ions (H⁺)** from the acid gain these electrons to form **Hydrogen gas** (reduction).
 
• In contrast, metals like **Copper**, **Silver**, and **Gold** are placed below hydrogen in the **reactivity series**. Because they are less reactive than hydrogen, they cannot displace it from dilute acids. ***Hence, these options are incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Reactivity Series:** 
 
 
• The **reactivity series** is a list of metals arranged in descending order of their chemical reactivity. Metals at the top, such as **Potassium (K)** and **Sodium (Na)**, are highly reactive and can react even with cold water.
 
• Metals located **above Hydrogen** in the series (like **Magnesium**, **Aluminum**, **Zinc**, and **Iron**) can displace hydrogen from dilute acids like **HCl** or **H₂SO₄**.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Hydrogen Gas:**
 
 
• The **Hydrogen gas** produced during the reaction is colorless and odorless. It can be identified using the **"Pop" test**: when a burning splinter is brought near the mouth of the test tube containing the gas, it burns with a characteristic **pop sound**.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Noble Metals:**
 
 
• **Gold (Au)** and **Silver (Ag)** are known as **noble metals** because they are chemically inert and do not react with ordinary dilute acids. **Gold** only dissolves in a special mixture called **Aqua Regia** (a **3:1** mixture of concentrated **HCl** and **HNO₃**).
 
• **Copper (Cu)** is also relatively unreactive and does not produce hydrogen with dilute **HCl**, although it may react with oxidizing acids like concentrated **Nitric acid**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Zinc Metal:** It has the **atomic number 30** and is commonly used in **galvanization** to prevent the rusting of iron. In the laboratory, **granulated zinc** is preferred for producing hydrogen gas because its larger surface area increases the **rate of reaction**.
 
• **Acid Strength:** While **Zinc** reacts with dilute **HCl** and **H₂SO₄** to give hydrogen, it does not typically produce hydrogen gas with **Nitric acid (HNO₃)**. This is because **HNO₃** is a **strong oxidizing agent** that oxidizes the produced hydrogen into **water (H₂O)** and itself gets reduced to nitrogen oxides.
 
• **Displacement Logic:** The ability of a metal to react with an acid depends on its **electrode potential**. Metals with a **negative reduction potential** (relative to the standard hydrogen electrode) are capable of liberating hydrogen gas from acids.
